introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in this question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One (booklet 0000/0595/3/Grp 1), Group Three (Grp 3) and Group Four (Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Group One: Task I (word processing, 15 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (HTML, 15 marks). Group Three: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 15 marks), Task 3 (HTML, 15 marks). Group Four: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (C or Pascal program, 10 marks). Each group is worth 50 marks.

The working files named in the tasks (pictures, logo, signature) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

**Task I (20 marks)**

Figure 1 is an extract of the timetable of a Form 4 class of GHS Tomtom. You are expected to study it carefully and then answer the questions that follow.

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2024-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_G4-T1_fig_1.png)

*Figure 1: the timetable, in a frame. At the top, the letter head in two blocks: on the left (English) REPUBLIC OF CAMEROON / Peace-Work-Fatherland, MINISTRY OF SECONDARY EDUCATION, REGIONAL DELEGATION FOR SOUTH WEST REGION, GOVERNMENT HIGH SCHOOL TOMTOM; on the right (French) REPUBLIQUE DU CAMEROUN / Paix-Travail-Patrie, MINISTERE DES ENSEIGNEMENTS SECONDAIRES, DELEGATION REGIONALE DU SUD OUEST, LYCEE DE TOMTOM. Then the title "NEW TIMETABLE FOR FORM 4" (underlined), the table below, and at the bottom "DONE AT TOMTOM THE ........" and "THE PRINCIPAL".*

Content of the table (row 1: the days; first column: the periods; the BREAK row is one merged cell across the five days):

| Time | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7h30-8h20 | Chemistry | English Language | French language | Mathematics | French language |
| 8h20-9h10 | Chemistry | English Language | French language | Mathematics | English Language |
| 9h10-10h00 | Mathematics | Computer science | Economics | English Language | Sports |
| 10h00-10h50 | Mathematics | Economics | Biology | Physics | Geography |
| 10h50-11h40 | Geography | Economics | Biology | Physics | Geography |
| 11h40-12H25 | BREAK |  |  |  |  |
| 12h30-13h20 | Computer science | Literature | Chemistry | French language | Citizenship |
| 13h20-14h10 | History | Physics | History | Additional mathematics/ Food and Nutrition | Citizenship |
| 14h10-15h00 | Biology | Manual Labour | Geography | Additional mathematics/ Food and Nutrition | Literature |

questions.enonce_markdown: 1. Write down the name of the word processor software installed in your computer. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The answer is the name of the word processing program that is **really installed on the candidate's computer**, for example **Microsoft Word**, **LibreOffice Writer** or **WPS Writer**. Look at the title bar of the program or at its *About* window to read its exact name.

Marking idea (1 mark): the name of a real word processing program (a spreadsheet or a text editor such as Notepad is not a word processor).

questions.enonce_markdown:
2. Identify 2 areas in Figure 1 where the following Word processing features could have been used. (You may consider that the document has the following areas: letter head, title, Column c where c is a number, Row r where r is a number, and signature area.)

a. Left alignment *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Left alignment** (text starting at the left edge of its area) is used in:

- the **letter head** block on the left (the English block: REPUBLIC OF CAMEROON, MINISTRY OF SECONDARY EDUCATION, ... GOVERNMENT HIGH SCHOOL TOMTOM);
- the cells of the columns Monday to Friday, where each subject (Chemistry, English Language, ...) starts at the left of its cell.

Any one valid area earns the mark.

questions.enonce_markdown:
2. Identify 2 areas in Figure 1 where the following Word processing features could have been used.

b. Center alignment *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Center alignment** (text in the middle of its area) is used in:

- the **title** "NEW TIMETABLE FOR FORM 4", in the middle of the page;
- the row of the **days** (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday), and the word **BREAK** in the middle of the merged row.

Any one valid area earns the mark.

questions.enonce_markdown: 3. Reproduce the document in Figure 1 using the word processor. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a new document and build the page from the top to the bottom.

1. **Letter head**: a block of text on the left (English) and a block on the right (French) placed side by side. The simplest way is a table of **2 columns and 1 row without borders**, one block of lines in each cell (the lines are centred under each other, as in the figure).
2. **Title**: type *NEW TIMETABLE FOR FORM 4*, centre it and underline it.
3. **Timetable**: insert a table of **6 columns and 10 rows** (1 heading row + 9 period rows). First row: an empty cell, then Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. First column: the nine periods *7h30-8h20, 8h20-9h10, 9h10-10h00, 10h00-10h50, 10h50-11h40, 11h40-12H25, 12h30-13h20, 13h20-14h10, 14h10-15h00*. Type the subjects of the table given above (Computer science, Literature, ...).
4. **BREAK row**: select the five cells to the right of *11h40-12H25* and click **Merge Cells**, then type *BREAK* in the merged cell.
5. **Closing lines** under the table: *DONE AT TOMTOM THE* followed by a line (type the underscore characters or a tab leader), and below it *THE PRINCIPAL*, both placed on the right of the page.

Check the spelling of the subjects and the times (for example *Additional mathematics/ Food and Nutrition* in the Thursday column on two periods).

Marking idea (6 marks, indicative): letter head (2); title (1); table with the right numbers of rows and columns (1); table contents correct (1); BREAK row merged and closing lines (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
4. Apply the following formatting:

- Font type: Arial or any other sans serif font *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the whole document (**Ctrl + A**) and choose **Arial** (or Calibri, Verdana...) in the font box. A sans serif font has no small strokes at the end of the letters (unlike Times New Roman). The whole document, including the table, must use it.

Marking idea (2 marks): a sans serif font chosen (1); applied to the whole document (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
4. Apply the following formatting:

- Letter head: Font size of 10 points *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the letter head (the two blocks at the top) and choose the font size **10** in the size box.

questions.enonce_markdown:
4. Apply the following formatting:

- Title: Font size of 16 points, bold *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the title *NEW TIMETABLE FOR FORM 4*, choose the size **16** and click **Bold** (Ctrl + B).

questions.enonce_markdown:
4. Apply the following formatting:

- Table and rest of document: Font size of 11 points *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Select the table (click its move handle at the top left corner) and the lines under it (*DONE AT TOMTOM THE ...*, *THE PRINCIPAL*) and choose the font size **11**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
4. Apply the following formatting:

- Column headings and row headings: bold *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the **first row** of the table (Monday to Friday: the column headings) and click **Bold**; then select the **first column** (the periods 7h30-8h20 ... 14h10-15h00: the row headings) and click **Bold**.

Marking idea (2 marks): column headings in bold (1); row headings in bold (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
4. Apply the following formatting:

- Table design and borders *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the whole table and apply **borders on all the cells** (Table Design > Borders > **All Borders**; or Table Properties > Borders and Shading > *Grid*), with a simple line style. Adjust the width of the columns so that the subjects fit, centre the text of the headings, and keep the BREAK row merged. The table then looks like the one of Figure 1 (a grid with a bold first row and a bold first column).

Marking idea (2 marks): borders on all the cells (1); neat design (column widths, alignment) (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: 5. Give two advantages of having an electronic copy of the timetable over a hand written copy. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two advantages (any two valid ones):

1. It can be **edited and updated quickly** (change a subject, a teacher or a time) without rewriting the whole timetable.
2. It can be **copied, printed many times and shared** (by e-mail, on a notice board or on a phone) for all the classes, whereas a hand written copy must be written again each time.

Other acceptable answers: it is neat and easy to read; it can be stored and backed up so that it is not lost or damaged; it can be formatted and checked for spelling mistakes.

Marking idea (2 marks): 1 mark for each valid advantage.

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task I and print
questions.corrige_markdown: Click **File > Save As**, type the name **Task I** and click **Save**. Then click **File > Print**, check the preview (the whole timetable must fit on one page) and click **Print**.
